11.text: COSMOGONICAL BELIEFS. — According to the cosmogonical beliefs of the

12.text: Chukchee, there are several worlds situated one above another, in such a

13.text: manner that the ground of one forms the sky of the one below. The num-

14.text: ber of these worlds is stated as five, seven, or nine. These worlds are

15.text: arranged symmetrically above and below the earth, each of the lower worlds

16.text: having a corresponding one above it.

17.text: According to a statement in the tale of “The Scabby Shaman,”¹ which

18.text: gives many curious details of the subject, there are four large worlds besides

19.text: the earth. Those nearest to the earth are occupied by keˊlet; the next, by

20.text: men. In the upper and lower worlds there are the same number of animals

21.text: on the land, birds in the air, and fish in the sea, so that the amount of

22.text: life is the same above and below the earth.

23.text: According to other statements, the lowest world is occupied by those

24.text: who have died twice, and therefore cannot return to earth. Some of these

25.text: worlds have several suns, the number of which varies from two to eight.

26.text: When it is winter in our world, it is summer in the next, and vice versâ.
26.note: §2.15 withdrawn: printed mark restored, read off the scan

27.text: According to the belief of the Koryak, the spirits in the world under us have day when it is

28.text: night here.² Likewise, the Oltcha of the Amur country believe that the “land of the deceased”

29.text: has winter when we have summer, and night when we have day. The inhabitants of the “land of

30.text: the deceased” have, moreover, plenty of game when it is scarce on the earth, and vice versá.³
